A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DisCoRD and have readable text, equations, tables and figures. The supplied v3 ends after the references, despite referencing supplementary material; v4 includes Supplementary Sections A–E. The comparison concerns the content actually supplied.

before.justification: Sections 4.2–4.3 report original motion reconstruction and generation experiments, component ablations, decoding measurements and human preference results.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and additionally reports residual-quantization experiments, decoder comparisons and further quantitative and qualitative evidence.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same condition projection, conditional rectified-flow decoder, windowed training and Euler inference procedure. Appendix A discloses implementation details without establishing a change to the proposed method; the alternative decoders are experimental comparisons.

E1.justification: Both versions cover text-to-motion on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, co-speech gestures on SHOW, and music-to-dance using AIST++ and HumanML3D. The added comparisons and examples use this existing coverage; quantization and sampler variations change configurations rather than tasks or domains.

E2.justification: Appendix Table B expands the text-to-motion comparisons with Fg-T2M, M2DM, M2D2M, MotionGPT, MotionLLM, MotionGPT-2 and AttT2M. Table E additionally compares DisCoRD with a DDPM decoder using DDIM sampling and a Linear SDE variant. These substantially broaden the reported comparator set.

E3.justification: New Table 5 varies MoMask residual-quantization levels across R=0,1,2,4,5. Appendix Table E adds controlled decoder and sampler comparisons at 2,16,50,100 steps. Appendix D additionally evaluates SHOW Diversity and Beat Consistency, and AIST++ kinetic/geometric FID and Beat Align Score. Existing-experiment settings newly disclosed elsewhere do not establish protocol revisions.

E4.justification: v4 adds direct tests of token representational capacity in Table 5 and decoder/sampler efficiency in Table E, plus additional trajectory and motion case studies. The earlier post-refinement, projection, attention and training-window ablations remain unchanged as Table 6; the earlier user-study findings are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions already report 95% confidence intervals and 20 timing trials. Appendix C.4 newly documents averaging per-sample Pearson correlations and excluding the lowest 10% of samples by human-score standard deviation. This clarifies statistical estimation behind the existing correlation claim without demonstrating additional runs or seeds.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and the original ablation table retain their numbers, while v4 adds substantial quantization, comparator, timing and supplementary results. Table D newly reports TM2D versus DisCoRD FIDk of 19.01 versus 23.98, FIDg of 20.09 versus 88.74, and BAS of 0.2049 versus 0.2190. These are mixed additional results, not performance changes between versions. Appendix C.4 supplies correlations of 0.181 and 0.483 behind the retained 2.7-times claim.

T1.justification: The rectified-flow formulation and total sJPE definition remain unchanged. Appendix C.2 expresses the previously described overestimation and underestimation components explicitly through max-based formulas and their sum. This algebraically restates the existing split without adding a substantive assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about DisCoRD, sJPE, compatibility with discrete motion frameworks and state-of-the-art performance, including FID values of 0.032 and 0.169. Added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly qualifies comparisons with ReMoDiffuse because of its specialized database and cautions that the additional dance metrics may disagree with actual motion quality. Table D explicitly acknowledges worse kinetic and geometric FID. The existing explanation connecting token capacity to faithfulness receives further support from the quantization study.

D1.justification: Appendix A/Table A newly supplies architecture dimensions, optimizer, learning rate, batch/window sizes, training budget and hardware/time. Other appendix sections document FGD scope, trajectory processing, study procedures and 41 participants in the preference study. A project website replaces the future code-release promise, although the PDFs do not establish actual code or checkpoint availability.

R1.justification: The related-work section and 67 bibliography entries remain substantively unchanged. Appendix D.1 adds a comparison qualification concerning ReMoDiffuse, and Table B broadens the named prior methods. Several added baseline citations appear as unresolved question marks.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose remains unchanged. v4 inserts the quantization discussion, shortens Section 4.3, relocates existing user-study discussion to the supplement, and adds acknowledgments and organized supplementary explanations. These are localized revisions and expansions rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v4 adds the quantization table, appendix implementation and comparison tables, additional trajectory and motion displays, and study-guideline/interface figures. v3 Figures 7 and 8 reappear as Figures F and E, while its Table 5 becomes Table 6. The combined additions and relocations substantially expand and reorganize the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 substantially improves reproducibility and scrutiny by supplying implementation and study details absent from the supplied v3, and by directly testing token capacity and alternative decoding choices. It also reports unfavorable dance metrics alongside favorable results, making the evidence more complete. Unresolved baseline citations and limited uncertainty reporting for new comparisons remain weaknesses, but the documentation and experimental gains resolve important deficiencies overall.
